subject: Clarify SLA for streaming vs batched endpoints — TTF and tokens/sec

Subject: SLA question — streaming vs batched endpoints (TTF / tokens/sec)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Acme is evaluating Redwood for our generative summarization pipeline. Before we move to procurement we need the SLA language tightened for two distinct workloads:

- Real-time user chat (streaming): low time-to-first-token (TTF) and stable token/sec while responding incrementally to users.
- Bulk document generation (non-streaming/batched): high throughput, predictable tokens/sec and clear tail latency for full responses.

Can you confirm the default SLA targets you offer for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints (TTF 95th/99th, tokens/sec sustained, and uptime)? Also, Acme is asking whether exceptions are possible for streaming (we expect many short sessions, TTF sensitivity) and what dedicated capacity / premium options look like.

I attached a short doc with our expected traffic patterns and two sample sessions (acme-sla-request.pdf).

Appreciate a clear table we can put into our SOW.

Best,

Hi Ana, Karthik —

Reviewed the attachment and Acme's session shapes. Below is a concise proposal you can drop into the SOW. This is intentionally prescriptive so procurement lawyers have concrete numbers.

Proposal (default Hosted API; deviations noted):

1) Non-streaming / Batched endpoints ("batch")
- Time-to-first-byte (start of response) is not as critical for batch since whole-response latency is the key metric. We propose:
  - Median full-response latency: <= 500 ms for single short responses (under 512 tokens) under normal load.
  - 95th percentile end-to-end latency: <= 1.5 s for responses < 1024 tokens.
  - Sustained throughput (tokens/sec aggregate per instance): a baseline of 1200 tokens/sec.
- Uptime: 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for Hosted API. Dedicated capacity available for 99.95% with SLA credits.

2) Streaming / Low-TTF endpoints ("stream")
- Time-to-first-token (TTF) expectations (measured from HTTP request accepted to first token byte streamed):
  - 95th percentile TTF: <= 120 ms (under expected session concurrency as provided).
  - 99th percentile TTF: <= 250 ms.
- Sustained token emission rate per stream: 200–500 tokens/sec depending on model and instance family; recommend we specify a conservative contractual floor of 180 tokens/sec for guaranteed paths and provide documented peak envelopes for higher burst.
- Uptime: streaming endpoints included in overall uptime SLA but note that end-to-end streaming reliability depends on network (client-side) and will be covered in the runbook.

3) Exception / Premium terms (what Acme asked for)
- For guaranteed TTF under 100 ms at 95th, we require Dedicated capacity sizing (reserved GPU pool) and a service onboarding run (~2 weeks) to tune kernels, batching, and prefix caching for Acme's session shapes.
- Premium SLA add-on: +0.05% uptime guarantee (e.g., 99.95% target) and a lower TTF floor; priced as a dedicated capacity uplift.
- Monitoring: we will ship token-level traces, TTF histograms, and per-session telemetry into a read-only dashboard (retention 90 days) as part of the premium package.

Operational notes:
- We measure TTF at the edge (Redwood ingress) and report both 95/99 percentiles daily.
- Credits for SLA misses: standard outage credit schedule applies; for premium packages we negotiate look-back windows and escalations.

Next steps: if Acme wants an exception to the standard Hosted numbers (e.g., 95th TTF <= 100 ms for streaming), we need a scope call and to size Dedicated capacity. Karthik — can you confirm Acme's expected concurrent streams and average session length?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups:

- Acme would like the 95th TTF for streaming to be contractually <= 100 ms if possible. We understand this likely needs Dedicated capacity; can you provide a ballpark uplift (monthly) for the capacity + SLA add-on?
- For tokens/sec, our worst-case load is many concurrent short sessions (~400 concurrent streams, average 30 tokens per response). Will that load fit the Dedicated sizing you referenced?
- Regarding credits: procurement asks for a formula that caps their financial exposure if TTF misses exceed thresholds for more than 2 consecutive days. Is that standard?

Also forwarding this to our procurement team for visibility.

Best,
Ana

Hi Ana — quick summary and next steps so everyone is aligned: 

1) Commitment: Redwood can offer the hosted defaults Marissa listed. For contractual 95th TTF <= 100 ms on streaming, we will need Dedicated capacity + onboarding.

2) Sizing ask (Acme input required): please confirm concurrent streams (you mentioned ~400) and average session length (tokens). We'll run a Dedicated sizing pass and return a monthly uplift estimate.

3) Credits / financial exposure: standard SLA credits apply for Hosted; for the premium package we can discuss a tailored credit formula that caps exposure after consecutive-day misses (procurement likes a look-back and a cap). We will provision a draft clause.

4) Pilot: propose a 2-week canary on Dedicated capacity (small reserved pool) to validate TTF and tokens/sec before full commit. If pilot metrics meet the 95th=100 ms target, we roll the full Dedicated sizing.
